chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Abu Sa'id, from Abu Hamza, who said:

We were a group in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). He called for food that we had no prior experience of being so delicious and fragrant. We were served dates so clear and beautiful that we looked at our own faces in them. A man said, 'We will surely be questioned about this bounty with which we have been favored in the presence of the son of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is more generous and noble than to feed you food, make it palatable, and then question you about it. But He will question you about what He has favored upon you through Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family).'
ai.seo_question: What is the primary basis for divine accountability according to Imam al-Sadiq: material sustenance or spiritual guidance?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the principle of *al-Ni'mah* (blessing) versus *al-Hisab* (accountability), asserting that Allah’s generosity precludes holding servants accountable for the mere consumption of sustenance. He redirects the focus of divine reckoning toward the spiritual privilege of recognizing and following the Prophet and his Ahl al-Bayt, which serves as the true source of favor. This distinction highlights the Shia theological emphasis on *Ma'rifah* (gnosis) of the Imams as the primary metric for reward, rather than material consumption alone.

en.hubeali: A number of our companion, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Usman Bin Isa, from Abu saeed, from Abu Hamza who said,

‘We were in the presence of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> as a group, so he<sup>asws</sup> called for the meal what in our time had never been any more delicious like it, and good, and came to us with dates, such that we kept looking at it and to our faces, from their cleanliness, and beauty. So a man said, ‘We would be Questioned about these Bounties which we have been favoured with in the presence of a son<sup>asws</sup> of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>’. 
So Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic is more Benevolent and Majestic that He<sup>azwj</sup> would Feed you food, so you justify it, then He<sup>azwj</sup> would Question you about it. But, He<sup>azwj</sup> would Question you about what He<sup>azwj</sup> has Favoured upon you by with Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> and the Progeny<sup>asws</sup> of Muhammad<sup>saww</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Khalid from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from abu Sa‘id from abu Hamzah who has said the following:

“Once we were in a group with abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam. He (the Imam) ordered such a food the like of which in good taste and elegance we had never seen. Thereafter dates were brought, in which we could see the reflection of our faces because of their clarity and goodness. A man then said, ‘We will be held accountable for these bounties that we have received in the house of the child of the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause. Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, then said, ‘Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, is honorable and glorious. Once He gives you food and makes it delicious, He then does not hold you accountable for it. However, He will ask you about what He has granted through Muhammad and Ale (of) Muhammad, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause.’”
